earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct Formosan language; only wordlists (Tsuchida 1985, Mueller 1910) per Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive descriptions.

sources.citation: Li, Paul Jen-kuei. 1993. New data on three extinct Formosan languages. BIHP 63.2: 301-323 (reprint in Li 2004, Selected Papers on Formosan Languages vol. 1, 91-108).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: p. 93 (sec. 2.1 Basay): 'Stress falls on the final syllable.' -- but this is for BASAY (basa1287; the language Abe/Ogawa used to call 'Ketangalan'), from a rememberer recorded in Jilung 1987; it does not cover Taipei-basin Ketangalan/Luilang (keta1243), which Li lists separately as extinct with <100 recorded items.

sources.citation: Li, Paul Jen-kuei (李壬癸). 2001. 巴賽語的地位 [The linguistic position of Basay]. Language and Linguistics 2.2: 155-171.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Subgrouping paper; explains that Ino's 'Ketagalan' should properly be called Basay (Mabuchi 1953-4, Tsuchida 1985) and that only a few lexical items survive for the Taipei-basin varieties. Nothing on stress (no 重音).

sources.citation: Tsuchida, Shigeru. 1985. Kulon: Yet another Austronesian language in Taiwan? Bulletin of the Institute of Ethnology, Academia Sinica 60: 1-59.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative wordlist study (Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description, 'wordlist or less'); Ketangalan = wordlists ##17-22 in the appendix. No stress rule anywhere; the only prosodic remark is p. 3 fn. 1: the kana/Chinese-character/roman records left by non-linguists are 'uncertain in regard to the distinction between b/m, l/r, medial and final t/l/r, and stress/length' -- i.e. stress is not recoverable from the surviving Ketangalan data.

sources.citation: Mueller, W. 1910. Ueber die Wildenstaemme der Insel Formosa. Zeitschrift fuer Ethnologie 42: 228-241.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Ethnographic overview; language content is one paragraph plus an appendix table of numerals 1-10 for all Formosan groups including a row 'Y) Ketanganan' (Tsa, Rusa..). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record keta1243 + English Wikipedia 'Luilang language', 'Basay language', 'Ketagalan people'.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Identity only: Glottolog links keta1243 to Wikipedia 'Luilang language', Glottolog's most extensive descriptions = Tsuchida 1985 and Mueller 1910 (both 'wordlist or less'), 0 descriptive refs. Wikipedia: 'probably went extinct in the mid-20th century and it is little researched'; only numerals (Guerin, Ino, Ogawa) cited. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Li, Paul Jen-kuei. 2024. Basay. In Li, Zeitoun & De Busser (eds.), Handbook of Formosan Languages: The Indigenous Languages of Taiwan. Leiden: Brill.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: publisher DOI, paywalled; library e-access not checked
sources.note: Most recent synthesis of all northern plains (Basay/Trobiawan/Ketangalan-Luilang) materials; if any modern author comments on prosody of the Taipei-basin variety or explicitly extends the Basay final-stress statement to it, it would be here. Low odds: Luilang data are <100 kana-recorded items.

sources.citation: Mabuchi, Toichi (馬淵東一). 1953-54. 高砂族の分類―学史的回顧 / on the naming Ketangalan vs Basai. 民族學研究 18.

sources.note: Source of the Ketangalan (= Luilang) vs Basay identity split that defines keta1243; ethnological, not expected to treat stress.

sources.citation: Ogawa, Naoyoshi (小川尚義). 1944. インドネシア語に於ける台湾高砂語の位置 [The position of the Formosan languages among the Indonesian languages]. In 太平洋協會 (ed.), 太平洋圏民族と文化 上巻, 451-503. Tokyo.

sources.note: Ogawa's own note separating 'Luilang' (= keta1243) from Ketangalan/Basay, with the Oat-a numerals he collected himself c. 1900; the only trained-linguist first-hand record of the variety. Unlikely to state stress but is the primary behind Tsuchida 1985.

sources.citation: Ino, Kanori (伊能嘉矩). 1896-1898. Reports on the Pepo of the Taipei area in 東京人類學會雜誌 [Journal of the Anthropological Society of Tokyo] (e.g. nos. 119-136), with Ketangalan wordlists in kana.

sources.note: The raw wordlists (##17-22 in Tsuchida's appendix) for Taipei-basin Ketangalan; open on J-STAGE but kana transcription cannot encode stress -- listed only for completeness of the primary record.
